Participants will learn how to maintain various aquaponic setups — systems that combine fish farming with hydroponic plant growth. Registration is $25, and attendees receive starter supplies to get growing.

The session is part of the Santa Rosa Farming Series, which offers a range of agricultural education workshops throughout the year. Interested growers can sign up through Eventbrite at https://www.eventbrite.com/e/santa-rosa-farming-series-tickets-1994985015886. For questions or accessibility accommodations, contact the extension office at 850-623-3868.

item.title: I-95 Interchange Opens Early in Indian River County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis celebrated the opening of a new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road in Indian River County on Monday, marking the completion of a major transportation project one year ahead of schedule. The interchange, Indian River County's first new I-95 connection in over 50 years, is expected to cut drive times in half for commuters using Oslo…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis celebrated the opening of a new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road in Indian River County on Monday, marking the completion of a major transportation project one year ahead of schedule. The interchange, Indian River County's first new I-95 connection in over 50 years, is expected to cut drive times in half for commuters using Oslo Road and reduce emergency response times along the interstate by up to 56 percent, according to the Governor's Press Office.

The project involved widening Oslo Road from two to four lanes and adding safety features including wrong-way vehicle detection technology, intersection lighting, and a new traffic signal. The interchange also includes sidewalks and bicycle lanes to accommodate pedestrians and cyclists. Beyond the immediate interchange improvements, the work created an evacuation route and aims to relieve congestion at existing I-95 connections at Indrio Road and State Road 60.

Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared W. Perdue credited the state's commitment to accelerating project delivery through innovative measures. The work also supported environmental conservation efforts by enabling the creation of a gopher tortoise habitat in the southwest quadrant of the interchange—described as the only such relocation site in southeast Florida. Officials highlighted the economic development benefits, noting that improved I-95 access strengthens freight movement along the designated truck route serving southern Indian River County.

item.content:encoded:
A Milton man has been sentenced to 45 months in federal prison after mailing a threatening letter while already incarcerated in a Florida correctional facility, according to WKRG News 5.

The sentencing was handed down on Monday as part of a federal case involving the threatening correspondence sent from within the prison system. Details about the specific nature of the threat or the intended recipient were not immediately available in initial reporting.

The case highlights ongoing concerns about contraband communication and security within Florida's prison system, where inmates have continued to pose threats from behind bars.

item.title: Milton to Host Downtown Revitalization Open House Thursday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton is inviting residents to weigh in on the future of downtown development at a public open house Thursday evening. Planning & Development will host the "PULL UP" Parking and Downtown Revitalization Open House at 5:30 p.m. at Milton City Hall, 6738 Dixon Street. The event comes after the city posed questions on social media about…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton is inviting residents to weigh in on the future of downtown development at a public open house Thursday evening. Planning & Development will host the "PULL UP" Parking and Downtown Revitalization Open House at 5:30 p.m. at Milton City Hall, 6738 Dixon Street.

The event comes after the city posed questions on social media about walkability and parking requirements, generating more than 300 comments from residents concerned about pedestrian safety, accessibility, and the overall vitality of downtown. Planning Director Jacob Hullett said the city wants to move those conversations from the comment section into a face-to-face forum. "We know how to draft city code, but we don't want to build Milton's future in a vacuum," Hullett said. "True community planning requires public engagement."

As Milton modernizes its development code, planners are reviewing parking requirements while also exploring long-term strategies for walkability, land use, and public spaces. At the open house, attendees can move between interactive displays, speak directly with city staff, ask questions, and share feedback on both parking policy and downtown's future direction. The city says everyone is welcome—whether you participated in the online conversation or have new ideas to contribute.

For more information, contact the City of Milton Public Information Office at (850) 983-5400 or PIO@miltonfl.org.

item.content:encoded:
Riviera Utilities crews responded to two sanitary sewage overflows in Foley, Alabama over the weekend, according to a news release from the utility company. The overflows occurred Sunday in the areas of South Juniper Street and Melbourne Court, sending wastewater into the Bon Secour River and Boggy Branch.

The utility did not immediately provide details on the cause of the overflows or the volume of sewage released. Residents in the affected areas may want to avoid contact with the waterways until additional testing can determine water quality.

Riviera Utilities has not yet announced whether boil water advisories or other precautions will be necessary for customers in those neighborhoods.

item.title: Jay Transfer Station Now Accepting Household Construction Debris
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Starting tomorrow, Santa Rosa County residents can bring small loads of household construction and demolition materials to the Jay Transfer Station, located at 3786 Transfer Station Road in Jay. The facility, open Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., will accept hand-unloadable items including lumber and wood scraps (no…
item.content:encoded:
Starting tomorrow, Santa Rosa County residents can bring small loads of household construction and demolition materials to the Jay Transfer Station, located at 3786 Transfer Station Road in Jay.

The facility, open Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., will accept hand-unloadable items including lumber and wood scraps (no treated wood), pipe, yard toys, wooden pallets, and acceptable household furniture—but not couches or mattresses. All materials must be safely manageable through normal transfer station operations, and customers are responsible for unloading everything themselves; staff cannot use equipment to assist.

The county emphasizes this service is designed for genuinely small loads from single residences. Oversized furniture, commercial quantities, items from multiple homes, or loads requiring multiple people or equipment to handle will be rejected. Facility staff will make the final call on acceptability based on size, quantity, type, and safety. Heavily loaded or multiple-residence materials should go to the Central Landfill in Milton instead. For a full list of accepted materials and guidelines, visit www.santarosa.fl.gov/960/Jay-Transfer-Station.

item.title: Alabama Lawmaker, School Board President Face Human Trafficking Charges
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Escambia County, AL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- An Alabama state representative and an area school board president are facing first-degree human trafficking charges following their arrests in Escambia County, Alabama. State Rep. Brett Easterbrook and Satsuma City School Board President Kory Wesley were booked into the Escambia County Detention Center…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County, AL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- An Alabama state representative and an area school board president are facing first-degree human trafficking charges following their arrests in Escambia County, Alabama.


State Rep. Brett Easterbrook and Satsuma City School Board President Kory Wesley were booked into the Escambia County Detention Center Friday afternoon.


Easterbrook, 63, represents Alabama House District 65, which includes Washington County and portions of Clarke and Baldwin counties.


He is charged with first-degree human trafficking and prostitution.

Wesley, 38, is charged with first-degree human trafficking and attempting to elude law enforcement.


Officials Release Few Details

Escambia County Sheriff Heath Jackson confirmed the arrests, but authorities have released few details explaining the allegations underlying the human trafficking charges.

Both men were released shortly after being booked. Jail records did not list their bond amounts.


The charges are allegations, and both men are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

Satsuma City Schools acknowledged Wesley's arrest in a statement, saying the school system would respect the legal process and would not comment on the allegations.

The district said it remains focused on serving its students, employees, families and community.


Orange Beach Official Also Arrested

A third public official was also arrested in connection with the multi-day undercover prostitution operation.


Orange Beach Public Works Director Timothy Tucker, 65, faces a prostitution charge.

The arrests give the case a direct Gulf Coast connection stretching from Mobile and Baldwin counties north into Escambia County, Alabama.


Authorities have not yet announced when Easterbrook or Wesley will make their first court appearances.

item.title: UWF respiratory therapy director wins top national educator honor
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Amanda Dexter, director of UWF's respiratory therapy program and assistant professor of clinical practice, has been named a 2026 Distinguished CHEST Educator by the American College of Chest Physicians. The award places her among the top 3% of CHEST faculty worldwide and recognizes sustained excellence in clinical education and leadership. Dexter…
item.content:encoded:
Amanda Dexter, director of UWF's respiratory therapy program and assistant professor of clinical practice, has been named a 2026 Distinguished CHEST Educator by the American College of Chest Physicians. The award places her among the top 3% of CHEST faculty worldwide and recognizes sustained excellence in clinical education and leadership. Dexter will be honored during the opening session of the CHEST Annual Meeting on October 18 in Phoenix.

The recognition is particularly significant because Dexter is a non-physician recipient—a distinction that Dr. Shelley Diviney, interim dean of UWF's Usha Kundu, MD College of Health, called "an even greater testament to Ms. Dexter's exceptionalism." Dexter has built her career around teaching, research, and global health work, traveling nationally and internationally to train clinicians and educators on high-fidelity medical simulators and respiratory care practices.

At UWF, Dexter oversees the university's B.S. Respiratory Therapy degree program, launched in 2025 as only the third such program in Florida. She manages accreditation requirements, coordinates advisory boards, and leads curriculum development while contributing to recruitment and community engagement efforts. "Teaching is one of the most rewarding parts of my career," Dexter said, adding that she hopes to inspire students "to embrace challenges and pursue opportunities with confidence."

item.title: Santa Rosa County Animal Services Offers Free Spay/Neuter for Community Cats
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County Animal Services is opening its doors for Community Cat Day twice this month, offering free spay and neuter services for stray and feral cats as part of a county-funded program. The program runs Thursday, October 15, and Thursday, October 29, at the shelter located at 4451 Pine Forest Road in Milton. Up to 50 cats will be accepted…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County Animal Services is opening its doors for Community Cat Day twice this month, offering free spay and neuter services for stray and feral cats as part of a county-funded program.

The program runs Thursday, October 15, and Thursday, October 29, at the shelter located at 4451 Pine Forest Road in Milton. Up to 50 cats will be accepted each day. Eligible cats must be at least three months old, outdoor, unowned, and free-roaming. Santa Rosa County residents can bring up to three cats per event and must provide proof of residency.

In addition to spaying or neutering, each cat will receive a rabies vaccination and an ear tip—a small notch that marks the cat as having been altered. Residents handle the trapping and transport themselves, dropping cats off at 8 a.m. and picking them up by 10 a.m. the following day. Cats must be transported in individual humane traps. Trap rentals are available starting October 12 and October 26 for $65, with a full refund upon return.

For more information on the program or other animal services, residents can visit www.santarosa.fl.gov/animals.

item.title: Tropical Depression Likely to Form in Gulf as Development Chances Jump to 70%
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The National Hurricane Center is watching a developing disturbance in the southwestern Gulf that could become a tropical depression later this week. As of early Monday, a surface trough of low pressure had developed along the Mexican coast in the southwestern Gulf. The Hurricane Center gives the disturbance a 30%…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The National Hurricane Center is watching a developing disturbance in the southwestern Gulf that could become a tropical depression later this week.

As of early Monday, a surface trough of low pressure had developed along the Mexican coast in the southwestern Gulf.


The Hurricane Center gives the disturbance a 30% chance of developing during the next 48 hours and a 70% chance over the next seven days.


Depression Possible Later This Week

Forecasters say environmental conditions are expected to be only marginally favorable for development.


However, gradual organization remains possible and a tropical depression could form during the second half of the week.


The disturbance is expected to initially drift east before turning northward.

At this point, there is no developed tropical cyclone and therefore no reliable track or specific impact forecast for Northwest Florida.


The National Hurricane Center's marine forecast says broader low pressure could develop over the far southwestern Gulf Tuesday night into Wednesday.


Regardless of whether a tropical depression forms, portions of the Gulf could experience increasing winds and rough seas later this week.


Northwest Florida Coming Off Wet Weekend

The system is worth watching as Northwest Florida comes off several days of heavy rainfall.

Southern Santa Rosa and Okaloosa counties remained under a flood advisory early Monday after two to three inches of rain fell in some areas overnight, with additional rainfall expected. The potential Gulf system is separate from the weather responsible for the weekend rainfall.


NewsRadio 92.3 will continue monitoring National Hurricane Center forecasts as the disturbance develops.
